questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical network policy design, validation, and rollback in a real namespace.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy scope and default-deny behavior
- Egress rules with podSelector/namespaceSelector and ports
- Validation with ephemeral test pods and service endpoints
- Rollback strategy if policy disrupts traffic

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: payments-egress-allow-redis
  namespace: payments
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: payments-redis
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 6379
```

```yaml
# Deny-all baseline (empty egress rules) with the same podSelector would also work
```

- How would you adapt this for multiple Redis replicas or region-like separation?
- How would you monitor and alert if legitimate egress is dropped after deployment?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical upgrade expertise: CRD versioning, conversion strategy, and zero-downtime controller upgrades.

- Deployment of updated controller image

## Why This Is Asked

- cert-manager Certificate and ClusterIssuer
- SecretName update triggers Ingress reload
- Renewal timing, ACME vs CA

```yaml
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: ingress-tls
  namespace: prod
spec:
  secretName: ingress-tls
  dnsNames:
  - app.example.com
  issuerRef:
    name: prod-cluster-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer
```

```yaml

kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: prod-cluster-issuer
spec:
```
